# convenience function to run count() for all of a vector of variables
count_df <- function(df, vars) {
  map(vars, 
      ~df %>%
        mutate_at(.x, ~labelled::to_factor(.x, levels = "prefixed")) %>%
        count(across(all_of(.x))) %>% 
        mutate(var = .x) %>% 
        rename(cat = .x) %>% 
        relocate(var)
      ) %>%
    bind_rows
}

10.10 labelled version of recode
This is an extension to the method from dplyr for labelled numeric data.
Although recode is called below with dplyr, this functionality is provided by labelled.

# Recoding with the labelled package
x <- labelled(1:3, c(yes = 1, no = 2))
x

<labelled<integer>[3]>
[1] 1 2 3

Labels:
 value label
     1   yes
     2    no

# Code below sets number 3 to be 2, and uses it's label.
dplyr::recode(x,`3` = 2L, .combine_value_labels = T)

<labelled<integer>[3]>
[1] 1 2 2

Labels:
 value label
     1   yes
     2    no


Where combined values have a label, these are combined…

x <- labelled(1:3, c(yes = 1, no = 2, maybe = 3))
x

<labelled<integer>[3]>
[1] 1 2 3

Labels:
 value label
     1   yes
     2    no
     3 maybe

dplyr::recode(x,`3` = 2L, .combine_value_labels = T)

<labelled<integer>[3]>
[1] 1 2 2

Labels:
 value      label
     1        yes
     2 no / maybe


A slightly realistic example

# Grouping agree / disagree style scale...
x <- labelled(
  1:4,
  c(
    "strongly agree" = 1,
    "agree" = 2,
    "disagree" = 3,
    "strongly disagree" = 4
  )
)

x

<labelled<integer>[4]>
[1] 1 2 3 4

Labels:
 value             label
     1    strongly agree
     2             agree
     3          disagree
     4 strongly disagree


Then, merge groups labels, .sep allows user defined break.

dplyr::recode(
  x,
  `1` = 1L,
  `2` = 1L,
  `3` = 2L,
  `4` = 2L,
  .combine_value_labels = TRUE, 
  .sep = " or "
)

<labelled<integer>[4]>
[1] 1 1 2 2

Labels:
 value                         label
     1       strongly agree or agree
     2 disagree or strongly disagree


Here recode drops value labels, so values are combined but labels dropped. Useful where combining labels is not helpful.

  `1` = 1L,
  `2` = 1L,
  `3` = 2L,

4.2.1 Refining ntile

# Function to add labels to ntile breaks
ntile_lab <- function(data, var, breaks = 5) { 
  
  var_to_use <- data %>% pull(var)
  
  vec <- ntile(zap_missing(var_to_use), n = breaks)
  
  breaks <- map(na.omit(unique(vec)),
                ~paste0(
                  min(zap_missing(var_to_use)[vec == .x],na.rm = T), " - ",
                  max(zap_missing(var_to_use)[vec == .x],na.rm = T)
                )
  )
  vec_unique <-  as.vector(na.omit(unique(vec)))
  names(vec_unique) <-  breaks
  vec_unique
  
  result <- vec %>% set_value_labels(.labels = vec_unique)
  
  return(result)
  
  }

4.3.3 Nice cut
This formats the output of cut. It assumes you’ll want the breaks to close on the right and include the lowest value in the sequence of breaks.
Access function: nice_cut.

nice_cut <- function(
    variable, 
    keep_user_na = F,
    breaks,
    dig_lab = 1, 
    lab_style = 1
){
  
  if(keep_user_na == F){variable <- labelled::user_na_to_na(variable)}
  
  new_variable <- cut(
    variable, 
    breaks, 
    include.lowest = T, 
    right = T, 
    dig.lab = dig_lab
    )

  cur_levels <- new_variable %>% levels()
  new_levels <- as.character(cur_levels)
     
   if(lab_style == 1){
     
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, "\\(|\\[", "Greater than ")
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, ",", " and up to ")

    } else if (lab_style == 2) {
      
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, "\\(|\\[", "")
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, ",", " > & <= ")

    } else if (lab_style == 3) {
      
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, "\\(|\\[", "")
     new_levels <- str_replace(new_levels, ",", "-")
     
    }

  new_levels <- str_remove(new_levels, "]")
  
  factor(
    new_variable, 
    levels = cur_levels,
    labels = new_levels
    )

}

writeLines(
  c("nice_cut <-", deparse(nice_cut, width.cutoff = 500)),
  file.path("Scripts/", "nice_cut.R")
)
